Connect your assistant to an internal app

Foundational 30 minutes Lab 1 of 3
Introduction
  1. On a call
    A customer asks how to return a broken blender. The RMA procedure is being migrated to Confluence — Maya knows it's there, somewhere.
    01
  2. Two minutes of hold music
    She tabs out, searches the wiki, opens the wrong page, then a closer one. The customer waits.

In this lab, you'll act as integration engineer for IDEA Brands — building the MCP server that gives Maya's AI assistant access to Confluence before the next customer calls. The lab data is synthetic — treat IDEA Brands as a real retailer.

MO
Maya Okonkwo
Tier-1 Support Agent · IDEA Brands

Mid-call, she needs the return policy. It's in Confluence somewhere — and the customer is still on the line.

The question

How do you give an off-the-shelf AI client access to systems it knows nothing about?

You'll learn how to

  • Connect a disconnected Confluence connection with an Atlassian API token
  • Stand up a pre-built MCP server and tell it when to use each tool
  • Register the server in an AI client (LibreChat) and attach it to a chat
  • Answer from a company standard operating procedure (SOP), then create and update a Confluence page

What you'll need

  • A Training Workato Labs Okta account (credentials emailed within the last 24 hours — search your inbox for Workshop Credentials)
  • Your assigned WOW##_MCP project, which already contains a disconnected Confluence connection
  • Access to the Librechat Application tile in the Okta portal
Phase 1

Connect the source of truth

In this phase, you'll connect a disconnected Confluence connection with an Atlassian API token.

Pattern

Authenticated connection

An MCP server can only reach what the underlying connection can reach. Before any tool works, the connection has to authenticate against the real system — here, Confluence Cloud via an Atlassian API token. The token is the credential; the connection is the reusable, audited path every tool shares.

1.1

Get into the training environment

Everything in this lab happens inside a training Workato workspace your trainer provisioned for the next 24 hours. Sign in through Okta first — the same single-sign-on the rest of the workshop runs on — and find your project.

Overview

Sign in to the Training Workato Labs Okta portal with the credentials emailed to you, then launch the training workspace tile — it's named for your event and ends in MCP Training Workspace. Inside Workato, open your assigned WOW##_MCP project — it already holds a Connections folder with a disconnected Confluence connection waiting for you.

Detailed steps 4 steps

This is pure orientation. No build yet — confirm you can reach your project and see the pre-seeded Confluence connection you'll wire up next.

  • Search your email for Workshop Credentials and open the message from the last 24 hours.
  • Sign in to the Training Workato Labs Okta portal with those credentials.
  • From the Okta dashboard, open the workspace tile ending in MCP Training Workspace.
  • From the left-hand navigation select Projects, then open your WOW##_MCP project and locate the Connections folder from the Assets tab.
Verify your WOW##_MCP project is open and the Connections folder lists a Confluence connection (named WOW### - MCP | [CSH] CON | Confluence) marked Disconnected.
1.2

Authenticate the Confluence connection

The Confluence connection ships disconnected on purpose — no shared password. You authenticate it with your own Atlassian API token, so every tool call the server later makes is traceable to you. Create the token, paste it in, connect.

Overview

Open the disconnected Confluence connection. Follow the id.atlassian.com link, create a fresh API token, copy it, and paste it into API token. The connection type, auth type, subdomain, and email are already filled. Click Connect and watch for the green badge.

Heads up

Copy the token the moment it appears — Atlassian shows it once and never again. If you close the dialog first, you'll make another one. New tokens can take up to a minute to start working.

Apply these values
FieldValue
Connection typeCloud
Auth typeAPI token
Confluence subdomaintraining-workatolabs
Emailatt###user@training.workatolabs.com
API tokenThe token you create at id.atlassian.com
Detailed steps 6 steps

An API token is a scoped, revocable password. Creating your own (rather than reusing a shared secret) is what keeps the audit trail honest once the AI client starts acting through this connection.

  • In the Connections folder, click the disconnected Confluence connection to edit it.
  • At the bottom of the connection form, click the id.atlassian.com link to open the Atlassian API token page in a new tab. Sign in with att###user@training.workatolabs.com if prompted.
  • On the API Tokens page, click Create API token.
  • Name the token WOW###MCPToken (replace ### with your number), leave the default one-week expiry, and click Create.
  • Click Copy to copy the token. You won't be able to view it again.
  • Back in Workato, paste the token into the API token field. Confirm the other fields match the config table, then click Connect.
Verify the right-hand panel shows a green Connected badge for the Confluence connection.
Phase 2

Stand up the MCP server

In this phase, you'll stand up a pre-built MCP server and tell it when to use each tool.

Pattern

Pre-built MCP server

You rarely build an MCP server tool-by-tool. Workato's pre-built Confluence MCP server ships a curated tool set (search, get, create, update, label, archive) plus sensible defaults, so you start from a working surface and prune. Server instructions are the other half: they tell the model what the server is for and how to sequence the tools.

2.1

Spin up the pre-built Confluence server

You could define MCP tools one at a time, but you almost never would — Workato's pre-built Confluence MCP server already ships a curated set (search, get, create, update, label, archive). The work here is less about assembling tools than starting from a working surface and pruning it down.

Overview

From your project, choose Create > MCP server. Search the pre-built servers for confluence, open the Confluence MCP server, and choose Use this server. Name the server Customer Support Hub, attach the Confluence connection you authenticated, and choose Start building.

Apply these values
FieldValue
CreateMCP server
Pre-built serverConfluence
Server nameCustomer Support Hub
ConnectionThe Confluence connection from Task 1.2
Detailed steps 6 steps

You'll trim the tool set in Lab 2 and tune descriptions in Lab 3 — for now, get a named server standing with the Confluence tools wired to your connection.

  • In your WOW##_MCP project, click Create (top-right) and choose MCP server.
  • On the Build your MCP server page, type confluence in the search field.
  • Open the pre-built Confluence MCP server and click Use this server to pre-populate the tools and settings.
  • Set Server name to Customer Support Hub.
  • Under Connections, click Connect to Confluence and select the connection you authenticated in Task 1.2.
  • Click Start building to finish.
Verify the Customer Support Hub server opens with a Tools section listing the Confluence tools (search, get, create, update, and more).
2.2

Give the server its instructions

Server instructions tell the large language model (LLM) what this server is for, when to search before answering, and which actions are out of scope — so it picks the right tool in the right order instead of guessing.

Overview

Download the ready-made instructions from FileStorage (Tools > FileStorage, then /Lab Assets/MCP-1/mcp-ex1-server-instructions.md). On the server's Overview tab, edit Server instruction and paste the file's contents in.

Note

Why instructions live on the server

The server instruction isn't shown to end users — it's read by the LLM. It frames the server's purpose, sets a tone ("help the support agent finish the task, not learn the plumbing"), and lays down rules like always search before answering a process question. Good instructions are the cheapest accuracy win you'll get.

Detailed steps 5 steps

Instructions live on the server, not inside any single tool. You'll grab a ready-made instruction file and paste it into the server's Overview, so every tool call inherits the same guidance.

  • In the left navigation, expand Tools and open FileStorage.
  • Open /Lab Assets/MCP-1/ and download mcp-ex1-server-instructions.md.
  • Return to the Customer Support Hub server (in the Customer Support Hub subfolder of your project).
  • On the Overview tab, click Edit on Server instruction.
  • Paste the contents of the downloaded file and save.
Verify the Server instruction section shows the pasted text describing the Customer Support Hub's purpose and tool-use rules.
2.3

Grab the server's address

Your server is live inside Workato, but no AI client knows it exists yet — and a fresh server has no access token. You mint one under Settings, and the copyable server URL that comes with it is the one thing LibreChat needs in the next phase.

Overview

Open the server's Settings tab — it lands on End user access. Under MCP Tokens, click Create new token, name it, and create it. A Copy server URL (includes token) dialog appears — copy that URL and stash it somewhere you can paste from in a minute; a scratch text file is fine.

Detailed steps 5 steps

The URL embeds an access token, so anyone with the link can reach the server. Treat it like a password for the duration of the workshop.

  • On the server, open the Settings tab — it opens on End user access.
  • Under MCP Tokens, click Create new token.
  • Name it WOW### LibreChat (token names are permanent) and click Create token.
  • In the Copy server URL (includes token) dialog, click Copy — the URL embeds your token and won't be shown again.
  • Paste it into a scratch text editor so it survives the next few steps, then click Done.
Verify you have a URL of the form https://####.apim.mcp.workato.com?wkt_token=… on your clipboard or in a scratch file.
Phase 3

Put your server to work in an AI client

In this phase, you'll register the server in an AI client (LibreChat) and attach it to a chat.

Pattern

Custom MCP client app

An MCP server is useless until a client connects to it. The client (LibreChat here, Claude in the appendix) reads the server's instructions and tool descriptions to decide what to call. Adding the server is the handshake; selecting it in a conversation is the activation.

3.1

Register the server as a custom MCP connection

Custom MCP servers don't show up in a client's built-in list — there's no install button. LibreChat's MCP Settings panel lets you add one directly, pointed at the server URL you copied from Workato.

Overview

Launch the Librechat Application tile from the Okta portal. Open MCP Settings from the left sidebar and click Add MCP. In the dialog, name it YourName MCP, paste your server URL, set Authentication to API Key and leave the key field blank, acknowledge the trust notice, and create it.

Heads up

The Name field only accepts letters, numbers, and spaces — no hyphens, so it's YourName MCP, not YourName-MCP. Checking "I trust this application" is LibreChat's version of a risk notice — you're vouching for a server nobody at IDEA has reviewed. Fine for this workshop; in production, IT publishes reviewed servers so users never see this checkbox.

Apply these values
FieldValue
NameYourName MCP
DescriptionIDEA Brands Customer Support Hub
MCP Server URLThe server URL you copied from the token dialog in Task 2.3
TransportStreamable HTTPS (default — leave as is)
AuthenticationAPI Key (leave the key field blank)
Detailed steps 6 steps

Adding the server is the handshake from the Phase 3 pattern — what makes it work here is API Key with a blank key field, because the token already lives inside the URL.

  • From the Okta portal, launch the Librechat Application tile.
  • Open MCP Settings from the left sidebar.
  • Click Add MCP.
  • Set Name to YourName MCP, Description to IDEA Brands Customer Support Hub, and paste the MCP Server URL from Task 2.3. Leave Transport on its default.
  • Under Authentication, select API Key and leave the key field blank — the token is already in the URL.
  • Check I trust this application and click Create MCP server.
Verify YourName MCP appears in your LibreChat MCP Servers list.
3.2

Ask the client what your server can do

The first proof the wiring works is the client reporting what your server can do — and that list comes straight from the instructions and tool descriptions you installed.

Overview

In the prompt bar, click MCP Servers and select YourName MCP so it appears as a chip below the prompt. Then ask What can YourName MCP do? and, to gauge the corpus, How many SOP pages are there in the WOW### space?.

Detailed steps 6 steps

Selecting the server scopes the conversation to its tools. The "what can you do" answer is generated from the texts you control — a quick sanity check that the client is reading your server, not improvising.

  • Start a new chat in LibreChat.
  • In the prompt bar, click MCP Servers and select YourName MCP.
  • If a dialog shows the server as Disconnected, click Initialize and wait for Active, then close it.
  • Confirm the server shows as selected in the prompt bar — that means it's active.
  • Ask What can YourName MCP do? and read the response.
  • Ask How many SOP pages are there in the WOW### space? (replace ### with your number).
Verify LibreChat describes the Customer Support Hub's capabilities and returns a count of SOP pages from your space. The exact count may vary run to run — what matters is that it searched your space rather than guessing.
Phase 4

Work a real support task

In this phase, you'll answer from a company standard operating procedure (SOP), then create and update a Confluence page.

Pattern

Retrieval and write-back

Read tools (search, get) ground the model in real content; write tools (create, update, label) let it act. The same server does both.

4.1

Pull a real SOP into the chat

This is the moment from the opening: a support question whose answer lives in the wiki. Ask it conversationally and let the server search Confluence, retrieve the page, and answer — no tabbing out.

Overview

Start with the Summarize all operational SOPs in WOW### prompt, then work through the suggestions below. Watch each reply for the search-and-read tool calls that precede the answer — that trace is how you tell grounding from guessing.

Try these
PromptWhat it exercises
Summarize all operational SOPs in WOW###Multi-page search + synthesis
Is there a deployment checklist? Can you boil it down for me?Targeted retrieval
How do I do a case handoff?Procedure lookup
How do I fix a shipping label?Procedure lookup
Tell me about our loyalty program.Topic retrieval
My manager asked me to do a post-incident review.Intent → doc match
Detailed steps 3 steps

No new configuration here — this is where retrieval pays off. Each prompt should make the client search Confluence and answer from a real page, so you can see grounding in action.

  • In your MCP-attached chat, send one of the prompts above.
  • Watch LibreChat call the search and read tools, then answer from the retrieved page.
  • Ask a follow-up that drills into the same SOP to confirm it's reading content, not improvising.
Verify the reply shows search and read tool calls and names or quotes the specific SOP page it answered from.
4.2

Turn a legacy PDF into a living wiki page

Retrieval is only half of what this server does — it can also create and update Confluence pages. Hand it a legacy SOP as a PDF and have it publish a clean, labelled page — then revise that page in place.

Overview

Download IDEA-SOP-RMA.pdf — a return merchandise authorization (RMA) SOP — from FileStorage. In LibreChat, use Attach File Options to upload it, then prompt Can you create a new page from this?. The model asks you some questions. Give your page a unique title like YourName RMA Page, and tell it to label the page RMA, SOP, and your own YourName-Label. Then push it further: update the figures, and bump the change log.

Try these
PromptWhat it exercises
Can you create a new page from this?Create page from PDF
Add labels: RMA, SOP, and "YourName-Label"add_labels
Actually that doc was a little out of date. Can you update all dollar amounts to be increased by 110%update_page
Did you update the change log for the RMA SOP? If not, bump the version and add an entry for the changes you made.update_page + reasoning
Detailed steps 6 steps

Write operations preserve Confluence's version history and stamp an audit comment naming the AI client and acting user — so an AI-authored page is as traceable as a human-authored one.

  • In Workato FileStorage, download IDEA-SOP-RMA.pdf from the MCP-1 Lab Assets.
  • In LibreChat, click Attach File Options and upload the PDF, then prompt Can you create a new page from this?.
  • When LibreChat proposes labels, reply Add labels: RMA, SOP, and "YourName-Label".
  • Prompt Actually that doc was a little out of date. Can you update all dollar amounts to be increased by 110%.
  • Prompt Did you update the change log for the RMA SOP? If not, bump the version and add an entry for the changes you made.
  • Close the loop from the opening: ask How do I process a return for a broken blender? — the page you published a moment ago answers it.
Verify each part lands: - Created — a new Confluence page appears in your space, its body built from the PDF. - Labelled — the page carries RMA, SOP, and your own YourName-Label. - Revised — the dollar figures changed. Check how they changed: "increased by 110%" can mean ×1.1 or ×2.1 to a model, the same way it can to a colleague. Whichever it picked, that ambiguity — and the follow-up you'd send to fix it — is the lesson. - Versioned — the change log shows a new version entry describing the edit.

Reflect

Now that you've built the integration, consider the tradeoffs you made.

  • You could chat with the server before writing good tool descriptions. What was driving its tool choices, and where would that go wrong at scale?
  • The server URL carries its own token. What's the operational risk, and how would you manage it outside a 24-hour workshop?
  • Every tool call the AI client made landed in Workato's job history and log entries — the observability plane of enterprise AI. Why does that record matter more when the actor is an AI client than when it's a person?
  • A teammate wants to expose every tool the Confluence connector offers "in case we need them." Make the argument for pruning instead.

Wrap-up

Maya's next customer call is shorter. She asks the AI client in the same window she's already in. It searches Confluence, reads the RMA SOP, and answers in one line — no tab-out, no hold music. And when a legacy PDF needs to become a wiki page, the same server writes it, labels it, and versions it.

Patterns to carry forward:

  • The connection is the trust boundary. Authenticate once; every tool reuses that connection, and every action traces back to you.
  • Start from a pre-built server, then subtract. A focused tool set beats an exhaustive one — the model chooses faster and more accurately.
  • Instructions are the cheapest accuracy win. Server instructions and tool descriptions are what the model reads to decide which tool to call, and in what order.
  • Read and write are one surface. The same MCP server grounds answers and takes action; your prompt decides which.

In Lab 2 you'll extend this server across Salesforce and Jira and watch the AI client reason across systems; in Lab 3 you'll tune the tool contract when it picks wrong.

Bonus challenges

Still have time? Push the server further.

  • Find a prompt where the model reaches for the wrong tool, then tighten that tool's description until it stops. LibreChat reads tool descriptions when it connects, so reconnect the server in MCP Settings, then re-test.
  • Ask for a summary that spans several SOPs, then check whether the answer names the specific Confluence pages it drew from.
  • Ask about a topic that isn't in Confluence. Does the server admit it found nothing, or does it guess? Note what you'd change in the instructions to make "I don't know" the honest default.
